title_en: The Supreme People's Court Notice on Issuing the "Opinion on Further Strengthening and Improving the Education and Training Work of People's Courts"
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Opinions on Further Strengthening and Improving Education and Training Work in People's Courts"

Fa Fa [2009] No. 7

To: Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The "Opinions on Further Strengthening and Improving Education and Training Work in People's Courts" are hereby issued to you for diligent implementation.

February 18, 2009

Opinions on Further Strengthening and Improving Education and Training Work in People's Courts

To further strengthen and improve education and training work in People's Courts, earnestly enhance the building of the People's Courts' contingent, and ensure the continuous improvement of the overall quality of the contingent, these Opinions are put forward in accordance with the "Judges Law of the People's Republic of China," the "Regulations on Education and Training of Cadres (Trial)," and the "Regulations on Judge Training," and in light of the actual work of People's Courts and the new requirements for education and training work in People's Courts in the new era.

I. Fully Recognize the New Situation and New Requirements for Education and Training Work in People's Courts in the New Era

1. Currently, China has entered a critical period of reform and opening up and building a moderately prosperous society in all respects. The responsibility of the People's Courts in serving development is more significant, and the task of safeguarding national security and social harmony and stability is more arduous. In the new era, the Party and the State have new requirements for the work of the People's Courts, and the people have new expectations for the work of the People's Courts. However, there remains a certain gap between the current state of the People's Courts' contingent and the requirements of the Party and the State as well as the expectations of the people. The quality and level of judicial work still need to be further improved. All court cadres and police officers, especially court leading cadres, must have a clear understanding of this. People's Courts at all levels must earnestly strengthen contingent building, improve the quality of the contingent, and ensure that the People's Courts provide more complete judicial services and stronger judicial guarantees for the State and the people.

2. The Party and the State have always attached importance to the education and training of cadres, consistently emphasizing its pioneering, fundamental, and strategic position. In his report to the 17th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC), General Secretary Hu Jintao called for "giving priority to education and building a country rich in human resources" and "building a learning society in which all people learn and pursue lifelong learning." Under the leadership of the CPC Central Committee, in recent years, the People's Courts have vigorously implemented the strategy of strengthening the court through talent, insisted on large-scale training of cadres and substantially improving the quality of cadres, and achieved notable results in education and training work, playing an important role in promoting court construction and judicial adjudication. However, some relatively prominent problems still exist in education and training work. In some localities, training focuses on professional skills while neglecting political aspects, or emphasizes knowledge while downplaying ability. Training is relatively lacking in specificity. Training for grassroots courts and courts in the western region is relatively weak. The training system and mechanism are not smooth enough, and the management system is not comprehensive enough. People's Courts at all levels must attach high importance to these issues and take effective measures to earnestly resolve them.

3. The guiding ideology for education and training work in People's Courts in the new era is: conscientiously implement the spirit of the 17th National Congress of the CPC, hold high the great banner of socialism with Chinese characteristics, take Deng Xiaoping Theory and the Important Thought of "Three Represents" as guidance, thoroughly implement the Scientific Outlook on Development, always adhere to the "Three Supremes," strive to practice the socialist rule of law concept, focus on strengthening ideals and beliefs, enhancing judicial abilities, and improving the capacity for scientific development, place greater emphasis on improving the quality and effectiveness of education and training, so that education and training work better serves the comprehensive, coordinated, and sustainable development of the courts and the healthy growth of the court contingent.

4. The main tasks for education and training work in People's Courts in the new era are: closely focusing on the new requirements of the Party and the State and the new expectations of the people, actively carrying out reform and innovation, strengthening training management, striving to build a pattern of large-scale education and large-scale training, continuing to train cadres on a large scale, substantially improving the quality of cadres, comprehensively enhancing the ideological and political quality, professional ethics, and comprehensive judicial capacity of the court contingent, and cultivating a contingent of courts that are politically steadfast, professionally proficient, have a fine work style, and administer justice impartially, so that all work of the People's Courts better serves the overall situation, better serves the people, better resolves conflicts, and better promotes harmony.

5. The principles that must be followed in education and training work in People's Courts in the new era are: adhere to a people-oriented approach and tailor teaching to needs; adhere to full-staff training with emphasis on key points; adhere to comprehensive development with a focus on ability; adhere to learning for application and seeking practical results; adhere to reform and innovation and scientific management.

II. Prominently Strengthen Ideological and Political Training

6. Ideological and political training must always be placed first as the top priority of court education and training work, and effectively improve the political quality and theoretical cultivation of court cadres and police officers. Unify understanding, thinking, and action on major issues such as what flag the court contingent raises, what path it takes, and for whom it administers justice and serves, to ensure the correct political direction of the People's Courts.

7. The major theoretical viewpoints and major strategic thoughts established by the 17th National Congress of the CPC, especially the Scientific Outlook on Development, should be made the key content of current court ideological and political training. Based on the actual work of the courts, in-depth education on the socialist rule of law concept should be carried out. Relevant courses should be offered in various types of training classes to ensure that these contents enter the textbooks, the classrooms, and the minds, are constantly taught with new perspectives, and ensure that everyone truly learns, truly believes, truly understands, and truly applies them.

8. Training on judge professional ethics, codes of conduct, and the construction of a clean and honest Party conduct should be strengthened to ensure that the court contingent administers justice fairly, civilly, and incorruptibly on the basis of adhering to the correct political direction, enhancing judicial credibility and improving judicial authority with a good judicial image.

9. Ideological and political education should be made a compulsory course for all types of training classes, and the spirit of the Central Committee should be promptly conveyed to every court cadre and police officer, guiding them to strengthen their ideals and beliefs, enhance Party spirit, and increase their sense of responsibility. Court cadres and police officers, especially the vast majority of Party members, are required to "uphold Party spirit, value moral integrity, and set an example." Ideological and political training should be focused on principal leading cadres and newly appointed leading cadres. In training classes for leading cadres, the proportion of ideological and political training content should not be less than 30%.

10. The methods of ideological and political education in People's Courts should be improved and innovated. People's Courts at all levels must closely combine their own realities and, according to local conditions, carry out education and training activities favored by the vast majority of cadres and police officers, such as essay competitions, exchange seminars, judge forums, and itinerant lectures, strengthen ideological guidance, and ensure that ideological and political education produces results and achieves practical effects. The Supreme People's Court shall organize the compilation of "Readings on Ideological and Political Construction of Court Cadres and Police Officers" as auxiliary teaching materials for ideological and political training.

11. The construction of academic style must be earnestly strengthened. Adhere to the integration of theory with practice, educate the vast majority of court cadres and police officers to continuously improve their ability to analyze and solve practical problems using Marxist positions, viewpoints, and methods, achieving the unity of theory and practice, learning and application, and words and actions, so as to work creatively.

III. Focus on Strengthening Judicial Capacity Training

12. Judicial capacity is a manifestation of the Party's governance capacity in the judicial field. The construction of judicial capacity in People's Courts is an important part of the construction of the Party's governance capacity. Full recognition should be given to the significance of judicial capacity cultivation for improving the quality of the People's Courts contingent. The judicial capacity training of court cadres and police officers should always be placed in an important position in the education and training work of People's Courts, effectively enhancing the ability of court cadres and police officers to distinguish legal principles and settle disputes, so that the People's Courts can better fulfill their duties.

13. Training on the "five capacities" of court cadres and police officers should be focused on: Training on the ability to understand and grasp the overall situation should be strengthened to further improve the overall situation awareness of court cadres and police officers, especially leading cadres, ensuring that all work of the People's Courts is carried out under the overall work of the Party and the State; training on the ability to understand and grasp social contradictions should be strengthened to further enhance court cadres' and police officers' understanding and comprehension of social issues and contradictions, enabling them to master the laws of mass work under the new situation and flexibly use mediation and adjudication methods to resolve social contradictions; training on the ability to understand and grasp public sentiment and the will of the people should be strengthened to further deepen court cadres' and police officers' observation and feeling of the people's hardships and public aspirations, ensuring that judicial adjudication pays attention to people's livelihood and safeguards the fundamental interests of the people; training on the ability to understand and grasp the spirit of the law should be strengthened to further enhance the level of court cadres' and police officers' understanding of legal provisions, the spirit of the law, and legislative intent, enabling them to correctly apply the law for mediation, adjudication, and enforcement, striving to achieve the organic unity of legal and social effects; training on the ability to understand and grasp new situations and solve new problems should be strengthened, so that court cadres and police officers further emancipate their minds, continuously innovate in work forms and content, and better adapt to the new requirements of building a harmonious society.

14. People's Courts at all levels must, in light of their own actual work, conscientiously study and summarize the laws and characteristics of judicial capacity cultivation for court cadres and police officers in the new era, vigorously promote the construction of learning-oriented courts, and enable court cadres and police officers to learn in practice and practice in learning. On the basis of continuing to focus on training the "four skills" of judges, namely, trial management, litigation mediation, legal application, and document drafting, activities such as on-the-job training, upward secondment and downward attachment, social investigation, and study tours should be widely carried out, encouraging court cadres and police officers to go deep into the grassroots, get close to the masses, and continuously improve their ability to solve practical problems and resolve conflicts and disputes. The Supreme People's Court shall organize the compilation of "Readings on Judicial Capacity Construction of Court Cadres and Police Officers" as auxiliary teaching materials for judicial capacity training.

15. Court training institutions must effectively change their training concepts, closely focus on the construction of the "five capacities," and further deepen teaching reform. Training content should be scientifically arranged, timely training on new laws and regulations, new judicial interpretations, frontier issues in jurisprudence, and other relevant knowledge should be provided, further broadening the theoretical horizons and knowledge areas of court cadres and police officers; training forms should be continuously innovated, flexibly using various methods such as case analysis, trial observation and simulation, and comment on legal documents, striving to achieve the transformation from knowledge-based training to ability-based training, from theory-based training to practice-based training, and from indoctrination-based training to interactive training, effectively enhancing the actual effect of training.

16. A judicial capacity evaluation mechanism should be established and improved, and the evaluation of court cadres' and police officers' judicial capacity should be effectively strengthened, using evaluation to promote learning and application. The Supreme People's Court shall study and formulate evaluation standards for the judicial capacity of court cadres and police officers, guide and supervise the development of judicial capacity evaluation work for court cadres and police officers nationwide. People's Courts at all levels shall, according to local conditions, carry out creative work around judicial capacity evaluation, thereby examining the effects of judicial capacity training and promoting the deepening of judicial capacity training.

IV. Increase Support for Education and Training in Grassroots and Western Courts

17. People's Courts at all levels should focus on cadres and police officers of grassroots courts as the priority for education and training, committing to implementing the requirements of promoting scientific development and social harmony at the grassroots level. The National Judges College, provincial-level court training institutions, and intermediate People's Courts shall, according to their respective responsibilities, carry out corresponding training for grassroots judges, ensuring that all cadres and police officers of grassroots People's Courts, including people's tribunals, receive a round of training every five years.

18. A variety of training support activities for courts in the western region should continue. Policies and funding should be tilted towards the western region and the old revolutionary base areas, ethnic minority areas, border areas, and poverty-stricken areas. Training for judges of ethnic minority languages and young and middle-aged judges in the western region should be strengthened, and attempts should be made to establish bilingual talent training bases in areas where ethnic minorities are concentrated.

19. The Supreme People's Court should regularly send lecturer groups to carry out itinerant lectures deep into grassroots and western regions, striving to solve practical problems such as shortage of training funds, insufficient teachers, and delayed information in grassroots and western regions, and timely provide training on the latest legislation, judicial interpretations, and hot and difficult issues in trial practice. Higher People's Courts at all levels should also carry out itinerant lecture activities according to local conditions, increasing intellectual support for grassroots levels.

20. Grassroots and western region courts should inherit and carry forward the fine tradition and style of hard work, fully tap their own potential, use existing conditions to encourage cadres and police officers to self-study, carry out various forms of training activities, create a strong learning atmosphere in the court, and enable cadres and police officers to improve through learning at work.

V. Further Establish and Improve Management Systems and Mechanisms

21. Education and training work must be conducted under unified leadership and centralized management. The political departments of People's Courts at all levels are the competent departments for education and training, primarily responsible for overall planning, macro guidance, coordination services, supervision and inspection, and institutional norms. The training institutions of People's Courts at all levels are the implementing bodies for education and training, primarily responsible for organizing and implementing various political and professional training for cadres and police officers. If trial and administrative departments have training needs, they shall report to the political department for unified planning, and be implemented uniformly by the training institutions. The competent departments for education and training and the training institutions must each perform their own duties, strengthen communication, cooperate closely, and form a joint force.

22. The competent departments for education and training should effectively play their functional role, take the lead in grasping the overall situation, strengthen supervision, and enhance management. They must firmly establish a service awareness, improve working methods, and increase work efficiency. They should promptly summarize and promote fresh experiences and effective practices of education and training reform and innovation, promptly discover and resolve existing problems, and promote the in-depth development of education and training work. People's Courts at all levels should strengthen the construction of education and training management teams, establishing a team of education and training managers who understand training, management, and trial, with excellent quality and sufficient quantity.

23. The construction of court training institutions should be further strengthened, especially the National Judges College and its branches. On the existing basis, funding should be increased and teaching conditions improved, fully leveraging the main role of the National Judges College in the education and training work of People's Courts. An open school-running model should be actively explored to mobilize the enthusiasm of court training institutions, improve the quality and efficiency of court education and training, and form a large training pattern of complementary advantages and positive interaction within the courts. All training institutions should adhere to the correct school-running direction, firmly establish the concept of serving trial work, reform school-running methods, and adhere to establishing the school with characteristics, invigorating the school with quality, and strengthening the school with brand.

24. Social resources should be fully utilized to broaden talent cultivation channels, cultivating high-level and compound talents for the courts. Attention should be paid to utilizing high-quality overseas education and training resources, adhering to the principle of taking China as the main body, using foreign resources for our benefit, avoiding disadvantages, and achieving greater effectiveness, to cultivate international talents for the courts. When cooperating with overseas entities, attention should be paid to political scrutiny and preventing infiltration by hostile forces.

25. A mechanism for evaluating and assessing training institutions should be established and improved. Evaluations should be conducted on the school-running policies, training quality, teaching staff, organizational management, infrastructure, and funding guarantees of court training institutions. For training institutions that fail to meet the evaluation standards, rectification within a prescribed period shall be ordered. The evaluation work shall be carried out every five years.

34. Efforts shall be made to improve the education and training assessment and incentive mechanisms, incorporating education and training into the court's performance evaluation system for excellence and merit, and conducting comprehensive assessments objectively on the leadership team's organization of education and training as well as the participation of judicial officers in education and training. The communication and coordination mechanism between training departments and personnel management departments shall be strengthened, and education and training shall be used as an important channel for cultivating, discovering, and identifying cadres. The assessment and evaluation results of judicial officers' training shall serve as an important basis for appointment and promotion, promoting the organic integration of training and utilization.

35. In accordance with the current fiscal system of China, active efforts shall be made to seek support from central and local finances, gradually establishing a two-level funding guarantee mechanism whereby the training expenses of the National Judges College are covered by the central finance, and the training expenses of provincial-level court training institutions are covered by the provincial finance. People's courts at all levels shall ensure the implementation of the funding standards set forth in the 2006-2010 National Plan for Judicial Education and Training, and gradually increase financial input into education and training as the economy grows.
